rationale.conceptual: The paper uses the well-established FLAPW-LDA method applied to a specific crystal structure. The task requires understanding how to set up DFT input, run SCF, and extract extremal orbits using SKEAF. While not novel, it demands careful handling of parameters (muffin-tin radii, k-point grids, Fermi surface mapping) that are non-trivial to translate correctly into working code.
rationale.execution: The reproduction involves at least four sequential stages: (1) prepare Elk input from crystal data, (2) run SCF on a moderate k-mesh, (3) run non-SCF on a finer mesh, and (4) run SKEAF to extract the required orbits and write the CSV. Each step requires managing dependencies and tool configurations (Elk, SKEAF). The pipeline is multi-stage but with well-defined, standard tooling, placing it at moderate orchestration difficulty.
